title: Slow-cooker smoky sausage and bean stew
subtitle: Smoked sausage with white beans in a paprika tomato broth
excerpt: Smoked pork sausage with cannellini beans, tinned tomatoes, and smoked paprika. A quick-prep one-pot that delivers a lot of flavour from very simple ingredients.
sourceNotes: Smoked sausage and bean stews are common across Eastern and Central European cooking, notably in Polish and Hungarian traditions. The smoked paprika and cannellini beans reflect both British and Spanish influences. No single canonical source.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Reheat on the hob with a splash of water.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Very good the next day. The smokiness deepens as the stew sits overnight.

content.text: The smoked sausage does most of the work here. It releases its fat and smoke into the broth during cooking and lifts the whole dish. Use a proper smoked sausage such as kielbasa, kabanos, or frankfurter-style pork sausage rather than a fresh sausage, which will lack the same depth.
Cannellini beans absorb the tomato and paprika broth well and go very creamy during a long cook. Slice the sausage thickly so it holds its shape. Thin slices will break apart.
Serve with crusty bread. A handful of wilted greens stirred in at the end adds colour.

Add the sliced {{smoked-pork-sausage}} of smoked sausage to the slow cooker with {{cannellini-beans}} of cannellini beans. Add {{onion}} diced onion and {{garlic}} of crushed garlic. Pour in {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes, {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree, and {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock. Add {{smoked-paprika}} of smoked paprika and {{bay-leaves}} of bay. Stir to combine.
Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 5 to 6 hours. Discard the bay leaves. Taste before adding {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt; the sausage will have contributed its own seasoning. Serve in deep bowls.

rows.symptom: The sausage has broken into small pieces
rows.cause: It was sliced too thin, or the slow cooker ran hot and the sausage cooked too fast.
rows.fix: Still tastes fine. Next time slice 1.5 cm thick. Or add the sausage in the last 2 hours if you want it to stay very intact.

rows.cause: The beans and tomatoes released more liquid than the slow cooker could reduce.
rows.fix: Set to HIGH with the lid off for 20 to 30 minutes. Or stir in a tablespoon of tomato puree.

rows.cause: Smoked sausage varies a lot in salt content. Some brands are very salty.
rows.fix: Add a small diced raw potato and cook for 20 minutes; it absorbs salt. Next time taste the sausage before cooking and adjust the seasoning accordingly.

rows.cause: The sausage was mild or lightly smoked.
rows.fix: Stir in an extra teaspoon of smoked paprika at the end.

content.text: Smoked sausage and bean stews appear across Central and Eastern Europe in various forms. In British cooking the same principle appears in dishes like sausage casserole, where a smoked or cured sausage carries a broth of tomato and beans. The slow cooker version takes about 10 minutes to assemble and produces a very satisfying winter dinner.
